Our LPC Associates

Finding Balance Counseling works as a supervised practice. Alongside Reem Glasco, LPC-S, a group of LPC Associates sees clients under her supervision, which means the same clinical lineage at lower fees and sooner availability. Sessions run $100 to $150 for a 50-minute individual session depending on the associate, and most hold a limited number of sliding-scale places from $70. Most work online across Texas; one also sees clients in person in Austin. Every associate offers a free consultation first.

Curious and warm, with the client setting the direction. Describes herself as sex-positive, shame-free about addiction, and an LGBTQIA+ ally, and offers nature-based sessions. Pronouns she/her.

$100 per 50 minutes, limited sliding-scale places at $70. Free 15-minute consultation.

M.A. in Counseling from St. Edward's University, with an internship completed at Austin State Hospital. Works with grief, emotional dysregulation, and symptoms whose roots sit in earlier experience, drawing on DBT, CBT, narrative work and EMDR principles. Bilingual in English and Spanish.

How to choose

Availability and fee decide it more often than specialty does. If you already know what you are bringing, the table above points at one or two people. If you do not, say what is going on in a few sentences through the contact page and you will be pointed at the right fit rather than left to guess.

You can also write to an associate directly. Every one of them offers a free consultation first, which exists precisely so that neither of you commits to a poor match.

What supervision means for you

An LPC Associate in Texas is fully qualified and licensed to practice, and is completing the 3,000 supervised hours the state requires before full licensure. Their work is reviewed every month by a Council-approved supervisor, which here means Reem.

In practice that means a second experienced clinician is thinking about your case alongside the person in the room. The licensure guide explains the requirement in full.

Questions about seeing an associate

What is an LPC Associate?

A counselor who has finished a master's degree, passed the required exams and holds a Texas LPC Associate license, and is completing 3,000 supervised hours toward full licensure. It is a license to practice, not a trainee status, and the work is supervised monthly by a Council-approved supervisor.

How much does it cost to see an associate?

$100 to $150 for a 50-minute individual session depending on the associate, and $150 to $165 for couples or family sessions. Most hold a limited number of sliding-scale places, starting at $70. Sessions with Reem herself are $240.

Do the associates have sooner availability than Reem?

Usually yes, and that is the main reason to start here. Reem keeps a small therapy caseload alongside supervising associates and consulting on EMDR, so her openings are limited and often waitlisted.

Is therapy with an associate as good?

It is different rather than lesser. An associate is earlier in their career and brings more open attention and a supervisor reviewing the work each month. Reem brings fifteen years and a particular depth in developmental trauma and stalled EMDR. For complex developmental trauma she is the better fit; for most other presentations an associate is a good one.

Can I see an associate in person?

Sheila Singh sees clients in person in Austin as well as by telehealth. The others work online across Texas. Trail walk and equine sessions are offered by Reem rather than the associates.

Do associates offer couples or family therapy?

Yes. Natasha Mahesh sees couples and families at $150 for 50 minutes, and Sheila Singh sees couples at $165. Reem's own caseload is individual therapy.

This practice does not provide emergency care. If you are in immediate danger, call 911. For a mental health crisis, call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
